name: loss-drivers
intro: The loss drivers a risk scenario prices, by loss category, the reporting level above them. Each driver says how much the attacker's dwell time changes its size (**Dwell sensitivity**) and the business quantity its amount scales with (**Scales with**), as the interface shows them. Every tenant gets this catalog at boot.

sections.title: Response & Investigation
sections.text: Investigating, managing and communicating the incident while it is being handled.

cells: External DFIR fees: scoping, containment, eradication, reconstruction and negotiation support.
Outside counsel under privilege, up to the point where claims are asserted.
External communications support; the cost tracks the public-visibility tier of the incident.
Incremental internal response cost: overtime, backfill and diverted staff, never counted again as lost productivity.

sections.title: Restoration & Rebuild
sections.text: Restoring systems and data, and replacing equipment that cannot be trusted again.

cells: Rebuild, reimage, restore, recreate data and revalidate, including the espionage-eviction rebuild.
Capital cost of physically destroyed or untrustable equipment; absorbs all replacement capex whenever it is active.

sections.title: Business Interruption (own operations)
sections.text: Margin and extra operating cost incurred while the organization runs degraded or not at all.

cells: Contribution margin on revenue lost during the outage, net of recapture, stopping at restoration.
Extra expense to operate degraded: manual processing, temporary staffing and expediting.

sections.title: Extortion
sections.text: Amounts actually paid to the attacker to end the extortion.

cells: Amount actually paid for decryption, suppression or cessation, including transaction costs; never substituted with restoration.

sections.title: Direct Financial Theft
sections.text: Funds taken by the attacker and never recovered.

cells: Funds fraudulently transferred and not recovered; carries the principal the organization is out of pocket, absorbed or restituted.

sections.title: Affected-Party Notification & Protection
sections.text: Informing the individuals affected and protecting them afterwards.

cells: Determining and executing the notification of affected individuals, plus the call-centre surge.
Monitoring and restoration offered to affected individuals, where the exposed data reaches adversary hands.

sections.title: Legal, Regulatory & Contractual Consequences
sections.text: Defense, settlements, fines, card-brand assessments and contractual penalties following the incident.

cells: Defense-side fees once claims are asserted.
Amounts paid to claimants, beyond-principal only on funds categories, including litigated business damages.
Statutory penalties imposed by regulators, bounded by the applicable statutory caps.
Card-brand program assessments through acquirers: reissuance, fraud recovery, forensic investigation and non-compliance. All card economics flow here.
Service credits, delivery-failure penalties and unlitigated liquidated damages under security-breach clauses; litigated damages sit in settlements.

sections.title: Future Revenue Loss
sections.text: Revenue and margin lost after restoration, through customer attrition or eroded competitive advantage.

cells: Margin on customers lost after restoration, plus win-back spend. All reputation cash lives here, starting where lost downtime margin stops.
Future margin lost because strategic assets are in adversary hands; a stolen-IP mechanism, distinct from eroded trust.
